title: Burst Reserve Allocation vignettes — NA/EU/APAC Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a fresh approach for regional GPU capacity planning: an explicit burst-reserve lane (short-term burstable capacity) combined with a baseline committed pool and a warm-up onboarding runway. The goal is to give product and SRE teams a rapid playbook for handling 3x week-over-week growth windows while keeping cost shock controlled.

Summary (one-liner):
Define a small, vendor-diverse burst reserve per region (NA/EU/APAC) sized by tail-percentile concurrency and backed by automated warm-on triggers to reduce cold-start risk during product-driven surges.

Key assumptions (callouts):
- Forecast horizon: 6 months (Jul 2026 — Dec 2026) with weekly cadence for first 8 weeks.
- Sequence-length distribution baseline: 70% short (<=128 tokens), 25% medium (128–1024), 5% long (>1024) for chat workloads. Long tails increase GPU memory pressure and KV-cache residency.
- Typical model mix per workload: halfling Llama-2-70B/q4f16 equivalents (quant-friendly) and the rest mixture of 13B/7B.
- Unit: 1 "GPU-unit" approximates an A10G-equivalent slot for throughput planning; adjust by kernel efficiency factor per region/vendor.
- Spot/Preemptible mix: target 20–40% of burst reserve, not for baseline.

Definitions used in the sheet:
- Baseline pool: committed/reserved capacity intended for steady-state traffic (monthly commit).
- Burst reserve: short-term capacity that can be spun up within minutes — a mix of spot + on-demand reserved warm nodes.
- Warm runway: small always-on fraction (10–15% of burst reserve) kept in a pre-warmed state to cut first-token latency.

High-level vignettes (scenarios):
1) Baseline growth (conservative): 10% monthly traffic growth. Trigger: weekly utilization > 70% for 2 consecutive weeks. Action: scale baseline pool by 10% next month, add 1 GPU-unit to burst reserve.
2) Product-initiated surge (expected): ~3x peak q-o-q for a 72-hour window. Trigger: feature rollout flag + metric spike. Action: activate burst reserve to full, promote 30% of burst nodes to warm-run mode (move from spot to short-term on-demand via vendor hot-lane).
3) Black-swan surge (unexpected, high risk): sustained traffic > 3x baseline for >7 days. Trigger: cross-team incident + exec decision. Action: expedite procurement and emergency on-demand capacity; enable cross-region routing (EU -> NA failover) and apply strict degradation policy (response truncation, lower temperature, reduced completion length).

Planned rollout timeline (weeks shown for initial 12-week runway starting 2026-07-01):
- Weeks 1–2: baseline sizing validation (traffic replay tests, kernel latency sweep), define warm-run images and golden AMIs/VMs.
- Weeks 3–4: vendor procurement windows (AWS/GCP/Azure spot pools reserved), automation for burst activation (Terraform + autoscaler blueprints).
- Weeks 5–6: deploy warm-run fraction (10% of burst reserve) and verify <50ms first-token on short sequences.
- Weeks 7–8: run 48–72h surge drills with synthetic traffic and split routing.
- Weeks 9–12: iterate sizing, update cost runbook, finalize runbook for on-call.

Capacity table (text CSV for quick import). Columns: region, vendor-lane, baseline-gpu-units, burst-reserve-gpu-units, warm-run-units, spot-target-%, expected-utilization-baseline-month1, expected-utilization-month3
NA, AWS, 400, 120, 12, 30, 55, 68
EU, GCP, 180, 60, 6, 35, 50, 64
APAC, Azure, 120, 48, 6, 30, 48, 62

Notes on numbers:
- Baseline corresponds to current committed capacity plus conservative add (5–10%) to avoid immediate cold starts.
- Burst reserve is sized to cover the 95th percentile short-term concurrency based on recent daily peaks (30–72h windows).
- Warm-run-units are ~10% of burst-reserve and should maintain hot KV caches for common prompts.

Utilization profiles and cost tradeoffs (short narrative):
- Keep baseline utilization target 45–70% to maintain latency SLOs. If baseline saturation drifts above 70% repeatedly, we convert part of the burst reserve to baseline via commit.
- The burst reserve should be charged at blended effective cost = on-demand-cost*(1 - spot-target) + spot-cost*spot-target + overhead (image warm-up time, autoscaler RPS).
- Runbook includes a quick calculation cell to compute blended cost per token for each region (linked artifact).

Failure modes and mitigations: 
- Spot evaporation during surge: mitigate by increasing warm-run fraction or pegging a small emergency on-demand pool (5% of burst reserve) in each region.
- Cross-region bandwidth bottleneck for large KV cache transfer: prefer local warm-run nodes; use cache routing to keep KV residency local.
- Vendor regional supply hiccup: last-resort cross-region routing + pre-warmed nodes in alternate cloud within the same geography.

Operational playbook (actionable steps on pager):
1) Pager triggers when region_utilization > 75% and error_rate uplift > 2x in 15 minutes.
2) Runbook step A: Activate burst reserve (automated). Confirm warm-run pool health checks within 3 minutes.
3) If latency still > SLO after 10 minutes, promote additional warm nodes (manual) and notify product for throttling knobs.
4) Documented rollback: scale burst back down gradually after 24h of stable decline to avoid flapping.

Open questions (notes to infra/product):
- Should the burst reserve be centrally billed or allocated to customer/team budgets? Current thinking: central infra budget for first 90 days of a feature launch, then chargeback.
- How aggressive should spot usage be for APAC where spot churn is historically higher? Propose a conservative 20% spot cap for APAC until we have 90-day reliability data.
- Can we automate warm-run promotion from spot to on-demand gracefully to avoid losing the cache? Need test plan.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Aisha: finalize warm-run image bake and health-check hooks (due 2026-06-10).
- Daniel: script surge-drill harness and synthetic traffic profiles (due 2026-06-20).
- Marisol: vendor engagement and short-term spot holds for burst lanes (due 2026-06-14).

Appendix — quick math example (one-line):
If NA expected 72-hour surge needs 3,000 concurrent short sequences and one GPU-unit handles 8 concurrent short sequences at desired latency, required units = ceil(3000 / 8) = 375 units. Baseline already has 400 units so NA is covered, burst reserve used for medium/long runs and overflow.

Notes to self (informal TODO):

- capture historical spot reclamation patterns per zone (GCP us-central1 preemptible history, AWS us-west-2 spot churn).
- link to telemetry query for 95th-percentile concurrency (CONFLUENCE-PLAT-4321).

End of sheet.
